# Data Report

All information on the data used in the project is compiled in the data report in order to ensure the traceability and reproducibility of the results and to enable a systematic expansion of the database.

The Ferrari Race Analysis Dashboard relies on Formula 1 race data provided through the FastF1 Python library. The raw data is fetched from the Ergast/OpenF1 APIs via FastF1, then filtered, cleaned, and enriched in the data acquisition layer before being visualised in the Streamlit application. This report documents the raw datasets, the processing pipeline, and the exploratory data analysis of both raw and processed data.

```{python}
#| label: setup
#| echo: false
#| output: false
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

import sys
from pathlib import Path

# ensure project root is on sys.path so imports work
project_root = Path.cwd().parent
if str(project_root) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(project_root))

import fastf1
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# set up fastf1 cache
cache_dir = project_root / "cache"
cache_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
fastf1.Cache.enable_cache(str(cache_dir))

# use a sample race for the EDA
SAMPLE_YEAR = 2025
SAMPLE_GP = "Bahrain Grand Prix"

session = fastf1.get_session(SAMPLE_YEAR, SAMPLE_GP, "R")
session.load(telemetry=True, weather=False, messages=False)
```


## Raw data

The project uses a single external data source — the **FastF1** Python library — which wraps the official Formula 1 timing data APIs. All race data (lap timings, telemetry, results, event schedules) is fetched at runtime through this library and cached locally for performance.

### Overview Raw Datasets

: Overview of raw datasets used in the project. {#tbl-raw-overview}

| Name | Source | Storage location |
|---|---|---|
| Event Schedule | FastF1 (`fastf1.get_event_schedule()`) | In-memory / local FastF1 cache (`cache/`) |
| Session Laps | FastF1 (`session.laps`) | In-memory / local FastF1 cache (`cache/`) |
| Session Results | FastF1 (`session.results`) | In-memory / local FastF1 cache (`cache/`) |
| Car Telemetry | FastF1 (`lap.get_telemetry()`) | In-memory / local FastF1 cache (`cache/`) |


### Details Event Schedule

- **Description**: Contains metadata for all events (races, sprints) in a given F1 season, including round numbers, event names, countries, and dates.
- **Data source**: FastF1 library, which fetches from the official F1 timing APIs.
- **Data procurement**: Call `fastf1.get_event_schedule(year, include_testing=False)`. The library handles API access and caching transparently. Any team member with `fastf1` installed can reproduce the data.
- **Legal aspects**: FastF1 is open-source (MIT license). The underlying F1 timing data is publicly available; no special licence is required for non-commercial and educational use.
- **Data governance**: Public data. No personal or business-sensitive information.

#### Data Catalogue

: Data catalogue for Event Schedule. {#tbl-schedule-catalogue}

| Column index | Column name | Datatype | Values (Range, validation rules) | Short description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | RoundNumber | int | 1–24 (depends on season calendar) | Sequential round number in the season |
| 2 | Country | string | Country names (e.g. "Bahrain", "Italy") | Host country of the event |
| 3 | Location | string | City names | City where the circuit is located |
| 4 | OfficialEventName | string | Free text | Full official event title |
| 5 | EventDate | datetime | Valid calendar dates within the season | Date of the main race |
| 6 | EventName | string | Free text (e.g. "Bahrain Grand Prix") | Short event name used for display |
| 7 | EventFormat | string | "conventional", "sprint_shootout", etc. | Weekend format type |
| 8 | Session1–Session5 | string | Session type names | Names of each session (Practice, Qualifying, Race, etc.) |
| 9 | Session1Date–Session5Date | datetime | Valid calendar dates | Local date/time of each session |


### Details Session Laps

- **Description**: Per-lap timing data for every driver in a race session. Includes lap times, sector times, speed trap readings, tyre compound information, pit stop timing, and track position.
- **Data source**: FastF1 library via `session.laps` after calling `session.load()`.
- **Data procurement**: Load a session with `fastf1.get_session(year, gp, "R")` followed by `session.load()`. FastF1 caches the fetched data locally. Reproducible by any team member.
- **Legal aspects**: Public timing data, MIT-licensed library. Educational/non-commercial use.
- **Data governance**: Public data. Driver names and team names are publicly known.
- **Variable classification**: `LapTime` / `LapTimeSec` are the primary dependent variables for performance analysis. All other columns serve as independent variables or contextual metadata.

#### Data Catalogue

: Data catalogue for Session Laps. {#tbl-laps-catalogue}

| Column index | Column name | Datatype | Values (Range, validation rules) | Short description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Time | timedelta | Positive duration | Cumulative session time at end of lap |
| 2 | Driver | string | 3-letter abbreviation (e.g. "VER", "LEC") | Driver identifier |
| 3 | DriverNumber | string | 1–99 | Car number |
| 4 | LapTime | timedelta | ~60s–180s (depends on circuit) | Total lap duration |
| 5 | LapNumber | int | 1–max laps (circuit dependent) | Sequential lap number |
| 6 | Stint | int | 1–5+ | Stint number (increments at each pit stop) |
| 7 | PitOutTime | timedelta | Positive or NaT | Session time when car left the pit lane |
| 8 | PitInTime | timedelta | Positive or NaT | Session time when car entered the pit lane |
| 9 | Sector1Time | timedelta | ~15–40s | Time for sector 1 |
| 10 | Sector2Time | timedelta | ~20–50s | Time for sector 2 |
| 11 | Sector3Time | timedelta | ~15–40s | Time for sector 3 |
| 12 | SpeedI1 | float | ~150–350 km/h | Speed at intermediate point 1 |
| 13 | SpeedI2 | float | ~150–350 km/h | Speed at intermediate point 2 |
| 14 | SpeedFL | float | ~150–350 km/h | Speed at finish line |
| 15 | SpeedST | float | ~150–370 km/h | Speed trap (max speed on straight) |
| 16 | IsPersonalBest | bool | True / False | Whether the lap is the driver's personal best |
| 17 | Compound | string | "SOFT", "MEDIUM", "HARD", "INTERMEDIATE", "WET" | Tyre compound used |
| 18 | TyreLife | int | 1–50+ | Number of laps on the current set of tyres |
| 19 | FreshTyre | bool | True / False | Whether the tyre set was new at the start of the stint |
| 20 | Team | string | Team names (e.g. "Ferrari", "Red Bull Racing") | Constructor / team name |
| 21 | TrackStatus | string | Status codes (e.g. "1" = green) | Track status during the lap |
| 22 | Position | float | 1–20 | Driver position at end of lap |
| 23 | Deleted | bool | True / False | Whether the lap time was deleted |
| 24 | IsAccurate | bool | True / False | FastF1 accuracy flag for the timing data |


### Details Session Results

- **Description**: Final classification of a race session, including finishing positions, grid positions, points scored, and retirement status.
- **Data source**: FastF1 library via `session.results`.
- **Data procurement**: Available after loading a session with `session.load()`. No additional API calls required.
- **Legal aspects**: Public race results. MIT-licensed library.
- **Data governance**: Public data. Contains driver names (public figures).

#### Data Catalogue

: Data catalogue for Session Results. {#tbl-results-catalogue}

| Column index | Column name | Datatype | Values (Range, validation rules) | Short description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | DriverNumber | string | 1–99 | Car number |
| 2 | BroadcastName | string | Free text | Name as shown in TV broadcast |
| 3 | Abbreviation | string | 3-letter code (e.g. "LEC") | Driver abbreviation |
| 4 | TeamName | string | Team names | Constructor / team name |
| 5 | FirstName | string | Free text | Driver first name |
| 6 | LastName | string | Free text | Driver last name |
| 7 | Position | float | 1–20 or NaN (DNF) | Final race classification |
| 8 | GridPosition | float | 1–20 | Starting grid position |
| 9 | Q1 | timedelta | Qualifying time or NaT | Qualifying Q1 time |
| 10 | Q2 | timedelta | Qualifying time or NaT | Qualifying Q2 time |
| 11 | Q3 | timedelta | Qualifying time or NaT | Qualifying Q3 time |
| 12 | Time | timedelta | Race time or NaT | Finishing time / gap to winner |
| 13 | Status | string | "Finished", "+1 Lap", "Collision", etc. | Race finish status |
| 14 | Points | float | 0–26 | Championship points awarded |


### Details Car Telemetry

- **Description**: High-frequency car telemetry data sampled at ~240 Hz for a given lap. Includes speed, throttle, brake, gear, RPM, DRS status, and 3D car position on track.
- **Data source**: FastF1 library via `lap.get_telemetry()`. Requires loading the session with `telemetry=True`.
- **Data procurement**: Load a session with `session.load(telemetry=True)`, pick a driver and lap, then call `get_telemetry()`. Initial telemetry load can take ~30 seconds.
- **Legal aspects**: Public timing data. MIT-licensed library.
- **Data governance**: Public data. High-frequency car performance data is publicly broadcast during races.

#### Data Catalogue

: Data catalogue for Car Telemetry. {#tbl-telemetry-catalogue}

| Column index | Column name | Datatype | Values (Range, validation rules) | Short description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Date | datetime | Timestamps during race | Absolute timestamp of the sample |
| 2 | SessionTime | timedelta | Positive duration | Time since session start |
| 3 | Time | timedelta | Positive duration | Time since lap start |
| 4 | RPM | int | 0–15000 | Engine revolutions per minute |
| 5 | Speed | int | 0–370 km/h | Car speed |
| 6 | nGear | int | 0–8 | Gear number (0 = neutral) |
| 7 | Throttle | float | 0–100 (%) | Throttle pedal position |
| 8 | Brake | bool/float | 0 or 1 (binary on/off, sometimes 0–100) | Brake pedal application |
| 9 | DRS | int | 0–14 (status codes) | Drag reduction system status |
| 10 | Distance | float | 0–7000+ m (circuit length) | Distance travelled from start/finish line |
| 11 | X | float | Track coordinates | Car X position on circuit |
| 12 | Y | float | Track coordinates | Car Y position on circuit |
| 13 | Z | float | Track coordinates | Car Z (elevation) position on circuit |


### Data Characteristics and Quality

The methods of exploratory data analysis are applied below using the sample race **2025 Bahrain Grand Prix** to characterise data quality and identify issues relevant to the visualisation design.

#### Laps Data — Exploratory Analysis

```{python}
#| label: fig-laps-profiling
#| fig-cap: "YData profiling summary statistics for the Session Laps dataset (2025 Bahrain GP)."
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true
#| output: true
from ydata_profiling import ProfileReport

# prepare laps for profiling (convert timedeltas to seconds for numeric analysis)
laps_raw = session.laps.copy()
for col in ["LapTime", "Sector1Time", "Sector2Time", "Sector3Time"]:
    if col in laps_raw.columns:
        laps_raw[f"{col}Sec"] = laps_raw[col].dt.total_seconds()

numeric_cols = [
    "LapNumber", "LapTimeSec", "Sector1TimeSec", "Sector2TimeSec", "Sector3TimeSec",
    "SpeedI1", "SpeedI2", "SpeedFL", "SpeedST", "TyreLife", "Position"
]
cat_cols = ["Driver", "Team", "Compound", "IsPersonalBest", "FreshTyre", "Deleted", "IsAccurate"]
profile_cols = [c for c in numeric_cols + cat_cols if c in laps_raw.columns]

laps_profile_df = laps_raw[profile_cols].copy()

profile = ProfileReport(
    laps_profile_df,
    title="Session Laps — 2025 Bahrain GP",
    minimal=True,
    progress_bar=False,
)

# save full report to docs/eda so it is deployed with the Quarto site
eda_dir = Path.cwd() / "eda"
eda_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
report_path = eda_dir / "laps_profile_report.html"
profile.to_file(report_path)

# display summary statistics
desc = laps_profile_df[numeric_cols].describe().round(2)
desc
```

[Open full interactive laps profiling report](eda/laps_profile_report.html){target="_blank"}


##### Missing Values Analysis

```{python}
#| label: fig-laps-missing
#| fig-cap: "Fraction of missing values per column in the Session Laps dataset."
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true
laps_full = session.laps.copy()
for col in ["LapTime", "Sector1Time", "Sector2Time", "Sector3Time"]:
    if col in laps_full.columns:
        laps_full[f"{col}Sec"] = laps_full[col].dt.total_seconds()

analysis_cols = [
    "LapNumber", "LapTimeSec", "Sector1TimeSec", "Sector2TimeSec", "Sector3TimeSec",
    "SpeedI1", "SpeedI2", "SpeedFL", "SpeedST", "TyreLife", "Position",
    "Compound", "Stint", "FreshTyre", "IsAccurate"
]
available_cols = [c for c in analysis_cols if c in laps_full.columns]
missing_frac = laps_full[available_cols].isnull().mean().sort_values(ascending=False)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4))
colors = ["#e8002d" if v > 0.05 else "#4C78A8" for v in missing_frac.values]
missing_frac.plot.barh(ax=ax, color=colors)
ax.set_xlabel("Fraction missing")
ax.set_title("Missing values per column — Session Laps")
ax.axvline(x=0.05, color="grey", linestyle="--", linewidth=0.8, label="5% threshold")
ax.legend()
ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

Key observations on missing values:

- **LapTime** and derived sector times can be missing for laps where timing was not recorded (e.g. in-lap, out-lap, red flag). The application handles this by calling `.dropna(subset=["LapTime"])` during processing.
- **Speed trap columns** (`SpeedI1`, `SpeedI2`, `SpeedFL`, `SpeedST`) may contain NaN when the speed trap sensor did not capture data.
- **Compound** and **TyreLife** are occasionally missing for the first or last lap of a stint.
- **Position** can be NaN for laps where the official classification was not yet determined.


##### Distribution of Lap Times

```{python}
#| label: fig-laptime-dist
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of lap times across all drivers and by tyre compound (2025 Bahrain GP)."
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true
laps_clean = laps_full.dropna(subset=["LapTimeSec", "Compound"]).copy()
# remove extreme outliers (SC laps, pit laps)
median_time = laps_clean["LapTimeSec"].median()
laps_clean = laps_clean[laps_clean["LapTimeSec"] <= median_time * 1.1]

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 4))

# overall distribution
axes[0].hist(laps_clean["LapTimeSec"], bins=40, color="#e8002d", edgecolor="white", alpha=0.8)
axes[0].axvline(laps_clean["LapTimeSec"].median(), color="black", linestyle="--", label=f"Median: {laps_clean['LapTimeSec'].median():.2f}s")
axes[0].set_xlabel("Lap Time (s)")
axes[0].set_ylabel("Count")
axes[0].set_title("Overall Lap Time Distribution")
axes[0].legend()
axes[0].spines["top"].set_visible(False)
axes[0].spines["right"].set_visible(False)

# by compound
compound_order = ["SOFT", "MEDIUM", "HARD"]
compound_colors = {"SOFT": "#ff3333", "MEDIUM": "#ffcc00", "HARD": "#cccccc", "INTERMEDIATE": "#33cc33", "WET": "#3399ff"}
for compound in compound_order:
    subset = laps_clean[laps_clean["Compound"] == compound]
    if not subset.empty:
        axes[1].hist(subset["LapTimeSec"], bins=25, alpha=0.6,
                     label=f"{compound} (n={len(subset)})",
                     color=compound_colors.get(compound, "#888888"), edgecolor="white")
axes[1].set_xlabel("Lap Time (s)")
axes[1].set_ylabel("Count")
axes[1].set_title("Lap Time Distribution by Compound")
axes[1].legend()
axes[1].spines["top"].set_visible(False)
axes[1].spines["right"].set_visible(False)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

##### Numerical Variable Correlations

```{python}
#| label: fig-laps-corr
#| fig-cap: "Pearson correlation heatmap of numerical variables in the laps dataset."
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true
corr_cols = ["LapTimeSec", "Sector1TimeSec", "Sector2TimeSec", "Sector3TimeSec",
             "SpeedI1", "SpeedI2", "SpeedFL", "SpeedST", "TyreLife", "Position", "LapNumber"]
available_corr = [c for c in corr_cols if c in laps_full.columns]
corr_matrix = laps_full[available_corr].dropna().corr(method="pearson")

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6))
sns.heatmap(corr_matrix, annot=True, fmt=".2f", cmap="RdBu_r", center=0,
            square=True, ax=ax, linewidths=0.5,
            xticklabels=[c.replace("Sec", "") for c in available_corr],
            yticklabels=[c.replace("Sec", "") for c in available_corr])
ax.set_title("Pearson Correlation — Lap Variables")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

Key observations:

- **Sector times** are strongly positively correlated with total lap time, as expected since lap time is the sum of sectors.
- **Speed trap values** show moderate negative correlation with lap time — faster cars tend to have lower (better) lap times.
- **TyreLife** shows a weak positive correlation with lap time, reflecting tyre degradation over a stint.
- **LapNumber** has weak correlation with most variables, indicating that lap performance is driven more by compound and fuel load than by lap count alone.


##### Lap Time vs. Tyre Life — Degradation Pattern

```{python}
#| label: fig-tyre-deg
#| fig-cap: "Lap time vs. tyre life coloured by compound, showing tyre degradation patterns."
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true
deg_data = laps_full.dropna(subset=["LapTimeSec", "TyreLife", "Compound"]).copy()
deg_data = deg_data[deg_data["LapTimeSec"] <= median_time * 1.1]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4.5))
for compound in ["SOFT", "MEDIUM", "HARD"]:
    subset = deg_data[deg_data["Compound"] == compound]
    if not subset.empty:
        ax.scatter(subset["TyreLife"], subset["LapTimeSec"], alpha=0.4, s=15,
                   color=compound_colors.get(compound, "#888"), label=compound)
ax.set_xlabel("Tyre Life (laps)")
ax.set_ylabel("Lap Time (s)")
ax.set_title("Tyre Degradation — Lap Time vs. Tyre Age")
ax.legend()
ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

##### Telemetry Correlations

```{python}
#| label: fig-telemetry-corr
#| fig-cap: "Spearman rank correlation heatmap of telemetry channels."
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true
tel_corr = tel_numeric[["Speed", "Throttle", "Brake", "nGear", "RPM"]].corr(method="spearman")

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 4))
sns.heatmap(tel_corr, annot=True, fmt=".2f", cmap="RdBu_r", center=0,
            square=True, ax=ax, linewidths=0.5)
ax.set_title("Spearman Correlation — Telemetry")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

Key observations:

- **Speed and Throttle** show strong positive correlation — the car accelerates with throttle.
- **Speed and Brake** show negative correlation — braking reduces speed.
- **nGear and Speed** are highly correlated — higher gears correspond to higher speeds.
- **Brake** is essentially binary (0 or 1) in most telemetry data, acting as an on/off signal rather than a proportional value.

#### Implications for Visualisation Design

Based on the exploratory analysis, the following implications are identified for the data processing and visualisation implementation:

1. **Missing lap times**: The raw laps dataset contains missing values for in-laps, out-laps, and safety car periods. The processing pipeline must filter these via `.dropna(subset=["LapTime"])` to avoid gaps in the lap time progression chart.

2. **Outlier laps**: Safety car laps, pit stop laps, and formation laps produce lap times significantly higher than normal racing laps. The application provides a "Hide SC / outlier laps" toggle that filters laps exceeding 107% of the median lap time.

3. **Tyre degradation**: The clear relationship between tyre life and lap time validates the degradation trendlines shown in the lap time visualisation. Dashed trendlines per stint are meaningful.

4. **Binary brake signal**: Since the brake telemetry is effectively binary, the track map visualisation uses it as a categorical overlay (on/off colouring) rather than a gradient, which is appropriate.

5. **Telemetry data volume**: A single lap produces ~500–1500 telemetry samples at ~240 Hz. Preloading telemetry via a background thread (`preload_telemetry()`) is essential for responsive user experience.

6. **Compound colour encoding**: The distinct tyre compound categories (SOFT, MEDIUM, HARD) with well-established colour associations (red, yellow, white) can be leveraged directly in strategy charts.

7. **Data availability**: The data quality is sufficient for the visualisation goals. FastF1 provides reliable timing data for completed races, with `IsAccurate` flags to identify potentially unreliable entries.


## Processed Data

The data acquisition layer (`data_acquisition/loader.py`) transforms the raw FastF1 data into focused, cleaned datasets for use by the visualisation modules. Each function applies filtering, column selection, type conversion, and feature derivation.

### Overview Processed Datasets

: Overview of processed datasets used in the project. {#tbl-processed-overview}

| Name | Source | Storage location |
|---|---|---|
| Ferrari Laps | `get_ferrari_laps()` — filtered from Session Laps | In-memory (Streamlit cache) |
| All Laps | `get_all_laps()` — filtered from Session Laps | In-memory (Streamlit cache) |
| Processed Results | `get_session_results()` — from Session Results | In-memory (Streamlit cache) |
| Processed Telemetry | `get_telemetry()` — from Car Telemetry | In-memory (Streamlit cache) |


### Details Ferrari Laps

- **Description**: Lap timing and tyre data for Ferrari drivers only. Used by the Home, Lap Times, and Track Map pages.
- **Processing steps**:
    1. Load session via `_load_session(year, gp, telemetry=False)`
    2. Filter to Ferrari team: `session.laps.pick_team("Ferrari")`
    3. Select columns: `Driver`, `LapNumber`, `LapTime`, `Compound`, `Stint`, `TyreLife`
    4. Drop rows with missing `LapTime`
    5. Derive `LapTimeSec` from `LapTime.dt.total_seconds()`
    6. Fill missing `Stint` values with `0`, cast to `int`
    7. Reset index
- **Access**: Call `get_ferrari_laps(year, gp)`. Results are cached by Streamlit (`@st.cache_data`).

#### Data Catalogue

: Data catalogue for Ferrari Laps. {#tbl-ferrari-laps-catalogue}

| Column index | Column name | Datatype | Values | Short description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Driver | string | 3-letter abbreviation | Ferrari driver identifier |
| 2 | LapNumber | int | 1–max laps | Sequential lap number |
| 3 | LapTime | timedelta | ~60–180s | Lap duration |
| 4 | Compound | string | "SOFT", "MEDIUM", "HARD", etc. | Tyre compound |
| 5 | Stint | int | 0+ (0 = unknown) | Stint number |
| 6 | TyreLife | int/float | 1–50+ | Laps on current tyre set |
| 7 | LapTimeSec | float | ~60–180 (derived) | Lap time in seconds |


### Details All Laps

- **Description**: Lap timing, tyre, and position data for all drivers. Used by Strategy, Lap Times, and Telemetry pages.
- **Processing steps**:
    1. Load session via `_load_session(year, gp, telemetry=False)`
    2. Select columns: `Driver`, `Team`, `LapNumber`, `LapTime`, `Compound`, `Stint`, `TyreLife`, `Position`
    3. Drop rows with missing `LapTime`
    4. Derive `LapTimeSec`
    5. Fill missing `Stint` with `0`, cast to `int`
    6. Reset index

#### Data Catalogue

: Data catalogue for All Laps. {#tbl-all-laps-catalogue}

| Column index | Column name | Datatype | Values | Short description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Driver | string | 3-letter abbreviation | Driver identifier |
| 2 | Team | string | Team names | Constructor name |
| 3 | LapNumber | int | 1–max laps | Sequential lap number |
| 4 | LapTime | timedelta | ~60–180s | Lap duration |
| 5 | Compound | string | Tyre compound names | Tyre compound |
| 6 | Stint | int | 0+ | Stint number |
| 7 | TyreLife | int/float | 1–50+ | Laps on current tyre set |
| 8 | Position | float | 1–20 | Race position at end of lap |
| 9 | LapTimeSec | float | ~60–180 (derived) | Lap time in seconds |


### Details Processed Results

- **Description**: Simplified race classification with numeric type conversions. Used by the Home page for KPI cards.
- **Processing steps**:
    1. Select columns: `Abbreviation`, `Position`, `GridPosition`, `Points`, `Status`
    2. Convert `Position`, `GridPosition`, `Points` to numeric (coerce errors to NaN)
    3. Fill NaN in `Points` with `0`
    4. Reset index

#### Data Catalogue

: Data catalogue for Processed Results. {#tbl-proc-results-catalogue}

| Column index | Column name | Datatype | Values | Short description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Abbreviation | string | 3-letter code | Driver abbreviation |
| 2 | Position | float | 1–20 or NaN | Final classification |
| 3 | GridPosition | float | 1–20 or NaN | Starting grid position |
| 4 | Points | float | 0–26 | Points scored (NaN filled to 0) |
| 5 | Status | string | Finish status codes | Race completion status |


### Details Processed Telemetry

- **Description**: Cleaned telemetry for a single driver-lap combination. Used by the Telemetry comparison and Track Map pages.
- **Processing steps**:
    1. Load session with `telemetry=True`
    2. Filter to specific driver and lap number
    3. Call `get_telemetry()` on the lap object
    4. Select columns: `Distance`, `Speed`, `Throttle`, `Brake`, `nGear`, `X`, `Y`
    5. Rename `nGear` → `Gear`
    6. Cast `Brake` to `float`
    7. Reset index

#### Data Catalogue

: Data catalogue for Processed Telemetry. {#tbl-proc-telemetry-catalogue}

| Column index | Column name | Datatype | Values | Short description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Distance | float | 0–7000+ m | Distance from start/finish |
| 2 | Speed | int | 0–370 km/h | Car speed |
| 3 | Throttle | float | 0–100% | Throttle position |
| 4 | Brake | float | 0–1 (cast from bool) | Brake application |
| 5 | Gear | int | 0–8 | Gear number |
| 6 | X | float | Track coordinates | X position on circuit |
| 7 | Y | float | Track coordinates | Y position on circuit |


### Processed Data — Quality Assessment

```{python}
#| label: fig-processed-quality
#| fig-cap: "Data quality comparison: raw vs. processed laps dataset."
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true
# simulate the processing pipeline
raw_laps = session.laps.copy()
ferrari_laps = raw_laps.pick_team("Ferrari").copy()
ferrari_laps = ferrari_laps[["Driver", "LapNumber", "LapTime", "Compound", "Stint", "TyreLife"]]

raw_count = len(ferrari_laps)
raw_missing_laptime = ferrari_laps["LapTime"].isna().sum()
ferrari_laps_clean = ferrari_laps.dropna(subset=["LapTime"])
clean_count = len(ferrari_laps_clean)

all_laps_raw = raw_laps.copy()
all_cols = ["Driver", "Team", "LapNumber", "LapTime", "Compound", "Stint", "TyreLife", "Position"]
all_laps_selected = all_laps_raw[all_cols]
all_raw_count = len(all_laps_selected)
all_clean_count = len(all_laps_selected.dropna(subset=["LapTime"]))

summary = pd.DataFrame({
    "Dataset": ["Ferrari Laps", "All Laps"],
    "Raw rows": [raw_count, all_raw_count],
    "After dropna(LapTime)": [clean_count, all_clean_count],
    "Rows removed": [raw_count - clean_count, all_raw_count - all_clean_count],
    "% removed": [
        f"{(raw_count - clean_count) / raw_count * 100:.1f}%",
        f"{(all_raw_count - all_clean_count) / all_raw_count * 100:.1f}%",
    ],
})

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3))
ax.axis("off")
table = ax.table(
    cellText=summary.values,
    colLabels=summary.columns,
    cellLoc="center",
    loc="center",
)
table.auto_set_font_size(False)
table.set_fontsize(9)
table.scale(1.2, 1.5)
ax.set_title("Rows before and after processing", fontsize=11, pad=10)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

The processing pipeline removes a small fraction of rows (primarily in-laps and out-laps without recorded times). No imputation is needed — the missing-time laps are genuinely incomplete and would distort visualisations if included. The remaining data is clean and sufficient for all visualisation features.
